title: Orders: any signed-in user can read another company's order
summary: A client from one company can open orders that belong to another company by id, in the API and in the Client Portal. This breaks the rule that different companies never see each other's data.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1 and POST /api/orders with reference QA-iso and one line (p-101, quantity 2); note the returned id
Sign in as bright-1 and GET /api/orders/{id} for that id (see evidence rules-I03 for the exact request)
Repeat as zain-1 (rules-I04)
In the Client Portal, signed in as zain-1, open order.html?id=<an Acme order id> and read the page title and contents (screenshots/zain-views-acme-order.png)
expected: HTTP 403 or 404 for an order of another company
actual: HTTP 200 with the full order for bright-1 and zain-1; the Client Portal shows the Acme order to a Zain user
suspected_cause: GET /orders/{id} does not compare the order's client to the caller's company (the list endpoint does filter correctly)

regression_test.description: As a client of company B, GET an order of company A and expect 403/404

title: Admin customers: any client can list every customer record with personal and payment details
summary: GET /api/admin/customers returns the full customer list to client accounts, not only admins. The records include contact details, an identity number, address, card digits and free-text notes for other companies.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
GET /api/admin/customers (evidence rules-R01)
Repeat as bright-1 (rules-R02)
Observe HTTP 200 with every company's record
expected: HTTP 403 for non-admin roles (config rule: only admins can see customers)
actual: HTTP 200 with all customer records. The role matrix shows 200 for all four client accounts, while /admin/reports/sales correctly gives 403
suspected_cause: Missing admin role check on the customers route

title: Orders: total is wrong on orders at or above 1,000.00 because tax ignores the discount
summary: Tax is calculated on the full subtotal instead of the discounted subtotal, so every discounted order is overcharged. The wrong total appears in the API, the order confirmation, My Orders and the Admin Portal.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders with p-102 x 80 (subtotal 1,000.00) (rules-T01); then p-104 x 1000 (subtotal 3,500.00) (rules-T04)
Compare the response with the rule: tax = 10% of (subtotal - discount)
In the Client Portal as acme-1, place an order of Ballpoint Pens x 80 with reference QA-ui-1 and read the confirmation banner
actual: 1,000.00: tax 100.00, total 1,050.00 (banner says $1,050.00). 3,500.00: tax 350.00, total 3,675.00. Orders below 1,000.00 are correct (989.89 gives 98.99 tax)
suspected_cause: src/pricing.mjs computes tax from subtotal rather than subtotal - discount

regression_test.description: Price a 1,000.00 order and expect tax 9500 and total 104500 cents

title: Sign-out: the token still works after signing out
summary: After POST /auth/logout returns 204, the same token still reads /me and /orders. A stolen or left-behind session cannot be ended.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-2
POST /api/auth/logout (204)
GET /api/me with the same token, then GET /api/orders (evidence rules-L02, rules-L03)
expected: HTTP 401 immediately after sign-out (config rule: signing out ends the session at once)
actual: HTTP 200 for both requests, 2 of 2 runs
suspected_cause: Logout does not revoke the token, or the auth check does not consult the revocation list

regression_test.description: Log out, then GET /me with the same token and expect 401

title: Orders: zero, negative, fractional and oversized quantities and empty item lists are accepted
summary: POST /orders accepts an empty items list and quantities of 0, -3, 1.5 and 1001, creating orders (one with a negative total of -21.45) that appear in both portals and in sales reporting.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders with items = [] (client-baseline-P043)
POST with quantity 0, 1001 and 1.5 (P044, P045, P046)
POST with quantity -3 (rules-T07) and read the negative total
expected: HTTP 400 (rule: whole number 1 to 1,000, at least one item)
actual: HTTP 201 each time; order created. The negative-quantity order shows -$21.45 in the Admin Portal list
suspected_cause: No server-side validation of items in the order handler

regression_test.description: POST orders with empty items and quantities 0, -1, 1.5, 1001 and expect 400

title: Orders list: page_size=0 and search text '(' or '\' return HTTP 500
summary: GET /orders crashes with a server error on page_size=0 and on searches containing an unbalanced bracket or backslash, so a client searching for such text gets an error. The spec says 400 for invalid input.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1 (or admin)
GET /api/orders?page_size=0 (P019)
GET /api/orders?q=( (P024) and ?q=\ (P028)
actual: HTTP 500 each time, 2 of 2 runs, as both roles. The same probes ran as admin: admin-baseline-P019, P024, P028
suspected_cause: The search text is used as a regular expression without escaping, and page_size 0 is not rejected

title: Orders list: page_size=-1 is accepted instead of refused
summary: GET /orders?page_size=-1 returns 200 and echoes page_size -1, which is outside the documented minimum of 1.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
GET /api/orders?page_size=-1 (client-baseline-P020)
expected: HTTP 400, or a clamp to a valid size
actual: HTTP 200 and page_size -1 in the body

title: API: malformed JSON returns a stack trace and server file paths
summary: Sending invalid JSON to POST /auth/login or POST /orders returns a 400 whose body includes a stack trace and source paths on the server.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with body {bad (client-baseline-P007)
As acme-1 POST /api/orders with malformed JSON (client-baseline-P048)
expected: A short 400 message without internal details
actual: 400 with stack and file paths in the body, 2 of 2 runs
suspected_cause: The error handler returns the error stack to the client

regression_test.description: Malformed JSON expects 400 and a body without 'stack' or file paths

title: Orders: submitting the same order twice at once creates two orders
summary: Two identical POST /orders sent in parallel both returned 201. The API has no duplicate protection, so a double click can place and bill two orders. The spec does not document duplicates as intended, so this is reported with that doubt.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
Send the same POST /api/orders twice in parallel (client-baseline-P049)
expected: One order, or a documented duplicate rule
actual: 201 for both requests in 2 of 2 runs

regression_test.description: Two parallel identical order POSTs yield one order

title: Sales report is slow: GET /admin/reports/sales takes about 4 seconds
summary: The sales summary takes 4.0 s every time, and the Admin Portal Reports page shows only a heading until it finishes.
steps: Sign in over the API as admin
GET /api/admin/reports/sales (admin-baseline-P061, admin-baseline-P093, sums-U02)
expected: Under 3 s on a small data set

regression_test.description: Sales report responds in under 3 s on the seed data

title: Client Portal (mobile 390px): My orders toolbar covers the first row and the Total column is cut off
summary: On a phone-width screen the Status filter and New order button overlap the top of the orders table, and the Total amounts are clipped inside a sideways-scrolling table.
steps: Set the viewport to 390x844
Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
Open My orders and look at the first row and the Total column (screenshots/client-myorders-mobile.png)
Reload and run the page audit: coveredElements lists the first row and the reference link
actual: The toolbar sits over the first row; totals such as $1,050.00 show truncated

regression_test.description: Layout check at 390px: toolbar does not cover the table

title: Portals: some controls have no accessible name
summary: Two icon buttons (refresh and clear filters) and the search box on the Admin Portal Orders page, and the product dropdown on the Client Portal New order page, have no label for screen readers.
steps: Sign in to the Admin Portal as admin and open Orders
Read the page snapshot: two buttons with no name; run the page audit at 390px (admin-orders-mobile.png)
Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1, open New order and run the audit: the product select is unnamed
expected: Every control has an accessible name

regression_test.description: Audit the Orders and New order pages for unnamed controls

title: Client Portal: Urdu order references show the hyphen on the wrong side
summary: For the Urdu company, references such as the Urdu word followed by a hyphen and 1044 appear with the hyphen at the left edge, because the text sits in a left-to-right cell. The audit reports 3 such cells. This may be a rendering preference; it reads oddly to an Urdu reader.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as zain-1
Open My orders
Look at the Reference column (screenshots/zain-myorders-desktop.png)
expected: Mixed Urdu and number text in a sensible visual order
actual: Hyphen displayed first, before the number, on 3 of 3 rows

regression_test.description: Render an Urdu reference with dir=auto and check order
